<!-- ============ DESCRIPTION ============ -->
::: {#description .sec}
## Description

Organised around topics, this course — together with its sequel, Economics of
Crime II — aims to equip students to read and critically evaluate the
literature on the economics of crime, with an emphasis on empirical work using
modern causal identification strategies. We discuss central questions in the
field: the effects of policing and the structure of punishment on criminal
behaviour, the consequences of immigration, the effectiveness of public policy
in illegal markets, and the dynamics of organised crime. Beyond becoming
familiar with the core literature, students will learn to recognise the limits
of existing evidence, identify open questions, and propose original research.
:::

<!-- ============ SYLLABUS ============ -->
::: {#syllabus .sec}
## Syllabus

::: {.topics}
1. Motivation: data, the state of the field, and empirical challenges
2. The rational choice model: static and dynamic
3. Police presence, enforcement, and discrimination in policing
4. Incarceration, monitoring, and punishment
5. Labour market conditions and education
6. Economic shocks and general equilibrium effects
7. Organised crime: causes and consequences
:::

A detailed reading list for each topic is available
[here](../files/reading-list.pdf){.pub-link}.
:::

<!-- ============ READINGS ============ -->
::: {#readings .sec}
## Main references

::: {.readings}
Lecture notes · Danilo Souza

Buonanno, P., P. Vanin, and J. Vargas (2022). *A Modern Guide to the Economics
of Crime*. Edward Elgar Publishing.

Chalfin, A. and J. McCrary (2017). Criminal deterrence: a review of the
literature. *Journal of Economic Literature* 55(1), 5–48.

Draca, M. and S. Machin (2015). Crime and economic incentives. *Annual Review
of Economics* 7, 389–408.

Cook, P. J., S. Machin, O. Marie, and G. Mastrobuoni (2013). *Lessons from the
Economics of Crime: What Reduces Offending?* MIT Press.

Benson, B. and P. R. Zimmerman (2010). *Handbook on the Economics of Crime*.
Edward Elgar Publishing.
:::

Selected journal articles are assigned for each topic.
:::
